findings.text: Hypervisor timer expiry for a vCPU checks whether hypervisor timing remains marked in use while preemption is held off, invokes expiration handling and withdraws hypervisor timing state, then advances and re-arms the next deadline when the timer is periodic with a nonzero period.

Timer backing moves between hypervisor and software modes: entering hypervisor backing restarts timing immediately, entering software backing starts software timing only when hypervisor timing was active, and restarting hypervisor timing expects hypervisor timing already active.

Memory mapped write entry validates the access lies in the mapped window, refuses or silently accepts accesses when hardware is disabled or extended mode is active depending on a compatibility quirk, ignores incorrectly sized or misaligned accesses, and forwards accepted word writes to register handling.
Host requested end of interrupt is expressed as a register write to the end of interrupt offset carrying a zero value.
Extended interrupt command register reserves bit thirteen, bits sixteen through seventeen, and bits twenty through thirty one.
Fast path for extended interrupt command writes delegates to shared command handling with fast behavior selected.

Decode free refresh requires an in kernel local APIC, treats the command register as one wide value in extended mode and through the legacy path otherwise, and rewrites the currently stored value so conditional adjustments still apply.

Deadline timer interface returns zero on read and ignores writes when the APIC is absent or not in deadline mode; a valid write cancels pending high resolution timing, records the new deadline, and arms the timer.
Task priority update from the control register keeps only its low four bits and places them in the upper nibble of the priority value.

Base updates store the new value, mark dynamic identification dirty when enable flips, adjust disabled tracking with asynchronous ready work on enable or dirty the optimized map on disable, refresh legacy or extended identifiers when mode bits flip, request virtualization updates and notify vendor logic when enablement changes, derive the mapped address, and inhibit acceleration when a non default base is enabled.

Base validation treats identical values as success, rejects nonzero reserved bits and invalid mode encodings, rejects guest initiated moves from extended to legacy and from disabled to extended, and otherwise applies the update and recalculates the optimized map.
Local APIC mode is derived solely from the enable and extended enable bits of the base value, with one helper reading the mode from a stored per vCPU base.

Acceleration refresh always marks request state pending, maintains service bookkeeping through vendor notification when active or by recounting service state when inactive, and invalidates the cached highest service vector.

Access page allocation serializes on the slot lock, succeeds immediately when already enabled or permanently inhibited, otherwise establishes the private region at the default address and records enablement.

Access page teardown uses a lock free enablement precheck, then releases vCPU read protection, acquires the slot lock, rechecks and deletes the private region, clears enablement before setting permanent inhibition, releases the lock, and reacquires read protection.
Per vCPU read protection records a lock index on entry and releases with the same index, with extra depth tracking when proving is enabled.

Reset seeds the base to default enabled with bootstrap indication except for init events, stops timers, restores identifiers version local vector entries priority error command timer divide and request service trigger state, conditionally restores legacy lint polarity for the bootstrap processor, refreshes virtualization metadata and attention state, and recalculates the optimized map.
Bootstrap identity at reset is decided by equality between the machine bootstrap identifier and the vCPU identifier.
Periodic timer status directly mirrors the timer vector configuration.
Memory mapped device operations bind separate read and write handlers for APIC accesses.
High resolution callback reports software timer expiry and, when periodic with nonzero period, advances the target deadline and re-arms itself, otherwise stops without restart.

Creation takes a no irqchip path without allocation, otherwise allocates control and register memory with vendor or zeroed page backing, initializes ownership vector count absolute timing enablement software disabled tracking and device operations, and optimistically enables acceleration with a deferred update.

Extended mode state translation enforces identifier match under strict format, repairs identifier and destination on set for compatibility, derives destination from identifier, and merges or splits the wide command value with legacy halves depending on vendor split support.

State save copies registers and refreshes the current timer count before translation; state restore handles priority enable separately, validates translation, copies registers, dirties and recalculates the map, refreshes version priority timer divide and watchdog state, restarts timing, synchronizes virtualization, and requests event evaluation.

Guest to host virtual APIC synchronization reconciles paravirtual end of interrupt state when its attention is set, then when checking is requested reads the cached guest word and updates task priority from its low byte.

Host to guest synchronization suppresses paravirtual signaling when disabled, when requests are pending, when the service cache is invalid, or when the IO path needs explicit notification, otherwise marks host pending; virtual APIC propagation packs priority with highest service and request values into the cached guest word when checking is requested.
Virtual APIC address setup initializes a guest cache and sets checking attention for a nonzero address, clears checking attention for a zero address, and records the address.
Extended register accesses translate the model specific number to a mapped offset, require an in kernel APIC in extended mode, delegate to register handling, and report unhandled otherwise.
Hypervisor expiry and software transition paths hold preemption disabled across in use checks and timer actions to synchronize with the preemption notifier.

Timer and register paths warn on blocking vCPU during hypervisor expiry, on restart without hypervisor timing active, on unexpected extended command results, and on periodic software expiry with zero period.

Memory mapped writes outside the window or with disabled hardware or extended mode without the hole quirk report not supported, while incorrectly sized or misaligned writes inside the window are silently ignored.
Memory mapped accesses use word length with sixteen byte alignment and select registers within the page; extended model specific numbers map to register offsets with a sixteen byte stride.
